word.note: Shin (three strokes) and lamed (ascender, bar and long diagonal) show. A crack crosses the word.

conduit.label: Aqueduct · Ilan–Amit 1989

features.label: Visible channel start · Ilan point 3
features.description: Best functional match for the head of the whole aqueduct. Located at a small ravine on the northern bank.
features.limit: No particular great stone identified. A northern bank does not resolve the wording’s grammatical ambiguity.

features.label: Branch junction and short western tunnel
features.description: Possible beginning of a collecting branch or subsection. Short tunnel probably corresponds to Reeder Tunnel 2.
features.limit: Needs a subsection-head reading. Branch function and flow direction differ among published interpretations.

features.label: Long eastern tunnel · western mouth
features.description: Reeder Fig. 2 and Magen Fig. 87 visually match the same long-tunnel mouth. Magen’s text supports its western/upstream attribution; Ilan point 11 and Reeder Tunnel 1 remain probable plan correspondences. Davey CJD979 supplies a matching 1974 view of this mouth.
features.limit: Downstream of the intake. Reeder calls the photo an exit and Magen an entrance; the visual match itself establishes neither hydraulic direction nor a scroll identity.
sources: Christopher Davey 1974, CJD979, DQCAAS photographic archive

features.label: Basin 2
features.description: The upstream basin in Ilan–Amit’s numbered aqueduct plan. It is distinct from the settlement pools.
features.limit: Its association with the named reservoir in entry 22 is conditional. No mapped fissure or geographic registration is established.

features.label: Proposed dam · point 4
features.description: A proposed lost dam across the east side of basin 2 in the source plan. Ilan–Amit 2002 Fig. 1 (p. 380) draws a heavy dashed line between points 3 and 4 across that side; the project reads it as probably the dam (drawing only; the text was not read).
features.limit: The authors report no surviving remains of a dam (1989 p. 284; p. 288 n. 5). Its existence and ancient phase are unresolved, and the dam/cairn reading remains disputed. The 3D model draws it as a copper-coloured reconstruction; its height and width are illustrative.
sources: Ilan–Amit 2002 Fig. 1, p. 380 (drawing only; owner's library photo, 19 Oct 2026)

conduit.credit: Project redrawing from the existing entry 21 comparison; manually sampled source-plan pixels.
conduit.limit: Source-relative geometry. Geographic registration is pending; highlight sizes do not represent positional accuracy.

cave.label: Abu Saraj · IV/17 cave
cave.credit: Ofer Sion / Israel Antiquities Authority · CC BY-NC 4.0. Complete Plan 5 figure crop; source caption, scale and north arrow retained.
cave.limit: No geographic registration. Complete published Plan 5 figure cropped from p. 63; no rotation or annotation baked into the image. Numbered selection markers are separate. The north arrow defines the right opening as northern. Present gaps do not reconstruct ancient thresholds, wall phases or floor elevations.

features.label: Northern opening · right side of plan
features.description: The source describes a 0.8 m northern opening leading into a northern space approximately 2.2 × 4.5 m.
features.limit: The northern member is distinguished using the drawn north arrow. Its present-aperture chord supplies no ancient threshold elevation or digging origin.
sources: Sion 2002 pp. 62–63, Plan 5; IV/17 assessment, 2 October 2026

features.label: Rock-cut dividing pillar
features.description: A rock-cut pillar divides the northern and southern spaces. Plan 5 shows an interior route around the pillar’s inner end.
features.limit: Two-dimensional connectivity does not establish ancient passage clearance. A pillar resemblance is shared with comparison caves and supplies no unique identification.

features.label: Southern opening · partial masonry block
features.description: The southern mouth is partly blocked by a masonry wall, reported as 2.4 m long and 0.4 m thick. The southern space is approximately 2.15 × 4.20 m.
features.limit: Present gaps differ from the earlier full mouth. Wall foundation, threshold contacts and a sealed construction date require the L-656 field file.
sources: Sion 2002 p. 63, Plan 5; IV/17 phase audit
